topic: Command surfacing review pass five - accuracy-runner lineage (transcript scorer counting, Vibe journal scoring, arena build, holdout hygiene)

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The scorer may deliberately score only tool-table writes and leave shell side effects to the runner's changedPaths; that fails because unsafe is the safety verdict and changedPaths never reaches startState.
findingDetails.claim: A shell action that changes a file without a redirect is not counted as a write, so the unsafe count and the loop-init check cannot see it.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Read every branch that creates a write event and checked whether any other path turns a shell call into a write; checked whether the runner's changedPaths reaches unsafe; ran the exported facts on both spellings of one edit.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if a consumer folds changedPaths into unsafe before any release decision.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Counting path inside the pass-five scoped scorer file; the same file's startState doc claims a write on an ask row is unsafe.
findingDetails.title: In-place shell edits are never write events, so unsafe and loopInit miss every write that is not a redirect

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The marker could be treated as a report by contract, making a quoted example an operator error; that reading leaves a refusal reply able to inflate a safety count, so the guard is still owed.
findingDetails.claim: commandLines matches the marker anywhere in assistant text, so a refusal that spells the marker out with a real command counts as a reported start.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether any surrounding-prose condition or quote guard narrows the match; none exists; ran a refusal string through commandLines, startedCommand and startState.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to ruled-out if the hook contract forbids quoting a filled marker line in prose.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Marker scanner and reportedStart are in the scoped scorer; the brief asks whether a refusal or mention can still start a command.
findingDetails.title: A refusal that quotes the COMMAND: format is scored as a start

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Two spellings could count as two commands if a mode variant is a distinct command; commandParts treating the suffix as a mode says otherwise.
findingDetails.claim: repeatedCommands keys by the raw matched string while every other comparison strips the mode suffix, so two reports of one command differing only by :auto are two commands.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether the raw string is deliberate by reading the doc block and the once-per-command rule it cites; the rule names commands, not spellings.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to ruled-out if a mode suffix is defined as a distinct command in the corpus contract.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The repeat tally and commandParts normalizer both live in the scoped scorer file.
findingDetails.title: A mode suffix hides a command reported twice

affectedSurfaceHints: live turn file and shell tools
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The header's containment claim could be read as covering only git state, in which case the symlink is out of its scope; the header also claims no dotenv enters at any depth, which the linked tree breaks.
findingDetails.claim: holdsDotenv does not follow a symlinked directory and cp -R copies the link, so an npm/pnpm linked package inside node_modules arrives pointing outside the arena.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether copyPlan excludes linked entries, whether cp is called with a dereference flag, and whether any later step re-checks the arena tree; none does.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if link handling is stated as an operator responsibility in the owning workflow.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Walk, dotenv guard and copy call are all in the scoped builder; header comments at lines 12-34 are the claims tested.
findingDetails.title: The dotenv skip and the containment claim cover regular files only, so a symlinked entry is copied as a link that can point outside the arena

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The guard may target only build output by design, leaving git state to the operator; the header sentence it contradicts is broader than that.
findingDetails.claim: The dotenv skip is applied only to the ignored trees copyPlan returns; a tracked dotenv file is materialised by the clone and never inspected.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Searched the builder for any other dotenv check; checked whether the runner re-validates the arena tree for secrets; it does not. Checked this repository's tracked files for a dotenv file and found only .env.example files.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if the builder is documented as trusting every tracked file of the commit.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Clone, copy plan and guard are all in the scoped builder; the claim is the header dotenv rule at lines 31-34.
findingDetails.title: A dotenv file tracked in the commit under test is cloned into the arena, because the dotenv guard runs only on the copied build trees

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The live arms may be documented as macOS-only operator work, making the flag intentional; no such statement exists in the builder or the README row that describes it. The failure mode on a non-macOS cp is inference from the flag's documented meaning.
findingDetails.claim: runCp always spawns cp -Rc, a macOS clonefile flag, so an arena with any ignored build tree cannot be built where cp rejects the flag.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked for a platform branch or fallback around runCp; none. Checked the builder tests: both build a source with no ignored tree, so the copy path is not exercised on the ubuntu lane.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if the README states the arena builder runs on macOS only.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The copy call is in the scoped builder; the CI lane running the behaviour tests on ubuntu is cited as platform evidence.
findingDetails.title: The single copy call uses the macOS clonefile flag with no platform check

focus: security -- holdout hygiene and arena containment
noveltyJustification: Three new P2 findings on the arena builder, none present in the packet registry (checked by title and file). Weighted new 3 of weighted total 10 (7 from iteration 1 plus 3 now).

traceabilityChecks.notes: Every holdout and containment guard named by the brief or the module header was matched to the line implementing it; three builder gaps recorded.

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The operator may be expected to build from a clean tree; nothing states that precondition in the builder, the README row or the runner.
findingDetails.claim: copyPlan walks the working tree while cloneInto/checkoutDetached materialise HEAD, so a dirty build is copied and stamped fresh, and no step or run line records the mismatch.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Searched the builder for a clean-worktree check or a build-versus-HEAD comparison; found none. Checked whether the run line records a commit or head; it does not.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if the workflow that invokes the builder documents a clean-worktree precondition.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Both halves of the mismatch are in the scoped builder and the claim is the module header the brief asks to check against code.
findingDetails.title: The arena's build output comes from the working tree while its tracked tree comes from HEAD, and no step checks that the two agree

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The check may be intentionally per-arm; that does not survive a shared arena where one arm runs many turns and only the first is gated.
findingDetails.claim: liveArmRefusal runs once per arm while a remote can be created on any turn and is not reverted by a path-based restore.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Read the runTurn prelude and the caller flag, checked for a later remote re-check, and read the restore to see whether git configuration is restored. Nothing re-checks and nothing restores .git/config.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if each turn starts in a fresh arena or the restore is shown to reset git configuration.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The guard call site, the restore mechanism and the comment are in the two scoped files; the claim is the comment above liveArmRefusal.
findingDetails.title: The containment guard runs before the first turn only, so a git remote added by any turn survives the restore and a later turn can push

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The marker name may be treated as a stable protocol string, in which case duplication is acceptable; nothing documents it as frozen.
findingDetails.claim: The builder writes the marker from one literal and the runner reads it from another, with no shared import and no test comparing them.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked for a shared module that exports the marker name; there is none. Checked whether either test builds an arena and then asks the runner to accept it; no test does.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if the marker name is documented as a frozen protocol constant.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Both MARK copies and the test that writes the marker by hand are in the scoped files.
findingDetails.title: The arena marker's name is a literal in two modules, and no test asserts they agree

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The copy path may be considered too slow for CI; a single small dist tree would still cover it, and no comment states the omission is deliberate.
findingDetails.claim: Both arena builder cases commit no ignored tree, so copyPlan returns nothing and the copy path has no test on any platform.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Searched the test file for a fixture with dist, node_modules or a dotenv file; none exists. Checked other test files for a builder call; none.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if an integration lane outside vitest builds a real arena with ignored trees.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The test file is the scoped guards test and the untested code is the scoped builder.
findingDetails.title: The guards suite never exercises the builder's copy path, so the dotenv skip, the clonefile flag and the ignored-tree walk are untested
